title: How Steve Jobs designed the first Apple Store: whole product line, try everything, ask a Genius
summary: Steve walks developers through the first Apple Store days before opening: the full product line in one quarter, hands-on digital devices, a Genius Bar for service, a theater, and software. The September 2001 email shows his leadership under crisis: put safety and people first, and lean on one another.

principles.text: Show the whole product line in one place so customers see the full picture.
principles.quote: Every product we make is in this first 25 percent of the store. You can see the whole product line.

principles.text: Let customers try products hands-on instead of just looking at them.
principles.quote: you can come in here, and not only can you buy these digital devices, but you can actually hook them right up to the Macs and take them for a spin.

principles.text: Build human expertise into the buying experience: put knowledgeable help in the store.
principles.quote: Wouldn’t it be great if when you went to buy a computer—or after you bought a computer—if you had any questions, you could ask a Genius?

principles.text: Back front-line staff with the company's deepest expertise, so no customer question goes unanswered.
principles.quote: if that person doesn't know the answer, they've got a hotline to call us in Cupertino at Apple headquarters, where we have somebody who does.

principles.text: Serve the whole ecosystem around your product, not only your own products.
principles.quote: We decided carrying our own products wasn’t enough, so we’re carrying six digital camcorders, six digital cameras, six MP3 players, and six handheld organizers.

principles.text: In a crisis, put people's safety first and tell the team to lean on each other.
principles.quote: Please take the time you need for your families, and please lean on one another. Together, we will all get through this.
